review:
Interesting game and very much deserving of all the awards it got. 

PROS:
- The story is one of the best ones i have seen in any videogame to date. Rivals my favorite games.
- The graphics are beautiful.
- The gameplay is good once you get the hang of it.
- The soundtrack is insane.
- Optimization of the game is decent, runs on a fairly budgeted rig on maximum settings. Could be better but isnt bad.
CONS:
- The combat system can be jarring at first, almost quit the game because i thought the parry system made the entire turn based combat redundant. It takes a lot of getting used to, but its a decent system. Expect a big difference if your previous turn based experience include a lot of classic Pokemon, Persona, etc.
- The character building system is kind of bad. Its very simplistic and lacks depth.
- The game kind of lags behind in other aspects, but those are usually minor faults. 
- The "open world overworld" is kind of lackluster. I get the point its making as being a "hub world", but still, feels like they could have expanded there.

Review:
With its innovative use of light and shadow, Clair Obscur Expedition 33 redefines the adventure genre and creates an immersive, intriguing, and alive world. This expedition is more than simply a trek; it's an artistic masterwork that combines cutting-edge gameplay mechanics with powerful visual storytelling, with each scene acting like a living chiaroscuro painting. Expedition 33's flawless blend of narrative complexity and perceptually challenging environmental challenges is what makes it genuinely exceptional and worthy of game-of-the-year honors. By changing light sources, players must navigate through shifting shadows and uncover hidden facts, transforming the idea of exploration into a unique sensory and intellectual experience. Clair Obscur Expedition 33's soundtrack creates an enthralling soundscape that draws you farther into the enigmatic universe of the game, making it incredibly addicting. The soundtrack's eerie melodies and ethereal tones enhance the emotional intensity at every step by flawlessly balancing the interaction of light and shade.

✅ Good
-Stunning Visuals
-Innovative Gameplay
-Addictive Soundtrack

❌ Bad
-Slow pacing

I've attatched my PC Spces - its not a budget build or something.

✅ Pros: Emotionally gripping narrative with deep themes, innovative turn-based combat with real-time parry/dodge mechanics, breathtaking Surrealist & Belle Époque art direction, phenomenal soundtrack and top-tier voice acting.
❌ Cons: Strict combat timing requirements can feel exhausting for some, linear world exploration with limited traversal options, lack of a minimap and minor visual lip-sync bugs.

[h1]Almost as good as the hype says - and that’s still pretty damn good.[/h1]

After watching Expedition 33 completely sweep the Game Awards, I couldn't really go into it with zero expectations. My main thought was honestly: “There is no way this game is THAT good.” 

While my expectations were met in that regard, I have to say overall the game is still fantastic. Since it has been glazed so much, I mostly want to break down both what makes it so special and the issues that I rarely see anyone talking about.

[hr][/hr]

[h1]What Makes the Game Phenomenal[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Incredible Music & World-Building:[/b] The soundtrack is mind-blowing, and the overall exposition and storytelling hooked me immediately and that is SO rare for me. I usually DGAF about the story of a game, sorry not sorry. I skip dialogue and cutscenes all the time, never read lore items but not with the this game. Quite the contrary. Even with the gripes I have later on, the overall story and lore are still genuinely great. (especially picking up the journals from previous expeditions!)
[*] [b]Fun Turn-Based Combat:[/b] I’m usually pretty neutral on turn-based RPGs (neither a huge fan nor a hater), but the combat in this game is straight forward and engaging. 
[*] [b]Stunning Art Direction & Visual Variety:[/b] Even if the technical graphics aren't super crisp (textures and resolution can look quite dated), the art direction completely carries it. The world is beautiful, and the enemy designs are visually diverse and so cool to encounter.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]1. Level Design & Traversal Flaws[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Annoying Navigation:[/b] The lack of a minimap really bothered me, along with having zero indication if you cleared an area or if you're under/overleveled. Dungeons can get on your nerves too: you’ll constantly see loot you can't reach, only to find out you have to progress to a completely different region just to loop back. Other games do this too but they do it better/ in a way that doesn't piss me off constantly. 
[*] [b]Weird level design & Clunky Hitboxes:[/b] Games usually give subtle visual cues to guide you, but here there are hidden areas with literally ZERO clues leading to them. I only found them through YouTube guides while going for 100%. Plus, platforming terrain hitboxes are sometimes very clunky. You'll cleanly jump onto a surface, touch an awkward slope, and just slide right off into the abyss. Really common with much older games, not something I would expect from a game that came out so recently. 
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]2. Story, Pacing & The Act 3 Problem[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]The Twist Kills the Spark:[/b] I’m a chronic cutscene-skipper in games, but Acts 1 & 2 had me hooked rushing to uncover the mystery. But the late-game reveal completely killed that momentum. [spoiler]Once the truth about reality comes out, that whole initial sense of wonder just evaporates into: "Oh... so none of this actually matters in the way I thought it did? This is all just because of some family drama?" The profound explanation was a little TOO profound for my own liking and I had a hard time caring about the Dessendre family drama. [/spoiler]
And this comes at the exact time where you can finally explore the world freely. My curiosity and wonder SHOULD be at an all time high at this point but unfortunately I just lost the motivation to explore because it all feels trivial.
[*] [b]Disconnect from Companions:[/b] Earlier on, the pacing is tight: you move from quest to quest, camp, talk with your party, and do their side stories. In Act 3, the map opens up, content gets super sparse, and you go hours without meaningful companion interactions. By the time you reach the finale, you feel a lot more detached from everyone. Which doesn't really help their case during the finale. 

So I am sure you can guess what ending I picked. When one falls we must continue.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]3. Combat Difficulty Balancing[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Optimized builds break the game:[/b] As fun as the combat is, once you figure out a solid build, the difficulty curve completely dies.
[*] [b]Avoiding side content STILL overlevels you:[/b] I actively tried NOT to overlevel for the final boss, so I skipped most side areas and only did companion quests and maybe two extra sections. Even then, my party became disgustingly overpowered.
[*] [b]Difficulty settings don't fix it:[/b] I ended up cranking the game to Expert with maximum challenge settings, and even as a casual gamer who isn't crazy good at games, it was still way too easy. Unless you artificially limit yourself by turning the damage cap back on, the endgame loses all sense of tension. (I defeated Simon on 100x life before he could take a single turn, i am not saying this to brag but to show how broken this is) I guess it's my own fault for making sure I don't leave any lumina behind.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]4. Male Gaze & Character Design[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Unrealistic Body Types:[/b] Every female body type in this game is essentially a tiny waist with big boobs, and the only "variety" is an even tinier waist with slightly smaller boobs. It’s not even about representation - body diversity builds realism. 
[*] [b]Form Over Functionality:[/b] Outfits are a huge part of characterizing someone, and here the design clearly prioritized catering to horny men over good characterization. Sciel was a farmer before this, yet she has a delicate, tiny frame and wears a crop top uniform showing off her midriff. Why isn't she built stronger? Why is her outfit so absurdly impractical? Why am I constantly seeing Lune's soles?!
[*] [b]Look at Nexus Mods if you think I'm reaching:[/b] If you think I'm reading too much into this, just go look at the sheer, absurd amount and popularity of NSFW/adult mods for this game on Nexus Mods compared to almost any other game. It speaks for itself.
[*] [b]Pointless Romance System:[/b] The romance options add absolutely nothing to the story or plot. It doesn't affect gameplay at all (which is nice if you want to skip it), but it’s so unnecessary that I literally forgot it existed. Choosing to romance a character doesn't make them behave any differently around you, you don't have additional interactions with the character, it's serves no purpose.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

Just wasn't for me:

- I didn't like the combat system (parry and dodge system is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and for some reason mandatory in Act 3 onwards because even if you spec every skill point into Defense and Vitality, many enemies are simply too powerful to realistically tank more than 2 or 3 hits). Although I eventually figured out the parry system and was able to do most of the content, having to memorize so many attack patterns and retry fights multiple times was a waste of time.
- I initially enjoyed the story, especially in Act 1 and most of Act 2, but the "twist" completely ruined any and all interest I had in the characters and it just didn't resonate with me. Kinda just made the whole game pointless imo
- Endgame content is simply too grindy, I didn't like it. Too much reliance on only 1 or 2 viable strats for several bosses, with very specific pictos or weapons which I just didn't find fun. I wish there were more viable options. 
- There is nothing that this game does particularly well or better than its competition. There is nothing new or interesting that this game innovated on. Everything is mediocre at best.

To be fair:
- Graphics are good and world design is impressive. 
- Animations, cutscenes, and voice acting are all very well done.

but this is not enough to make me like it overall.

All in all I strongly disliked the 2nd half of my playthrough and I quite resent having purchased this game. I had even avoided a lot of the hype and marketing, specifically because I wanted to give it a fair shot by going in mostly blind, but was very disappointed. If I could refund this purchase I would. 4/10

I find the game pretty good and well made.

The Good:
- I find the story engaging and well made, it was pretty cooked for the most part. I was excited being part of the expedition and wanted to progress the journey very much.
- The world is beautiful, it was much very fun to explore and just to look around.
- Combat mechanics are engaging most of the game. The parry feels great and the time events are clear for the most part and reward success.
- Combat visuals are very good, dopamine hits whenever you hit the enemy and parry.

The Bad:
- The biggest flow is you fight at most with 3 people while your party has 5, same would be for the enemy max 3 enemies.
- I did not like the world map, its too basic.
- The item system which you can pick up is very dull, it's basically currency, lumi/weapon upgrades and potions, there are no real items and at a certain point I just gave up even trying to reach for the hidden / hard to get items because the reward is poor.
- I personally did not like the weapon system, they spam you with weapons, at end game each character has like 15 diff weapons from a list, I would prefer modification and upgrades then this spam system.
- End game combat system became dull, I did praise the mechanic but at some point its just ugh annoying and not engaging anymore.
- Some of the dialogs are ugh poorly made.

I guess I can finally review this game after it has firmly landed in my "did not finish" pile.

I recommend it with a sort of forlorn feeling that suits this game.  E33 is beautiful, charming, full of charisma and bold choices.  There were times where I genuinely loved the game and even though I ended up not a fan, I appreciate what it was doing.

The turn-based combat is sleek and the world is aesthetically remarkable and original, but both of these are masking tedious or underbaked designs.  Once you learn all of an enemy's moves and how to counter them, the fights become sort of rote and you fall back on familiar strategies until the combat is over and you can move on.  Between combats, you move through dungeons or explore the over world map, but neither have particularly interesting challenges beyond being pretty zones to wander through between fights.

In other RPGs similar to this game, that might be patched over by a compulsion to finish the story.  But I found the story in E33 only compelling in spurts and by the time I entered the endgame portion, I felt it was kind of overdramatic and maybe even a bit boring.  There are some cool twists that happen along the way though, particularly the first major rugpull about 8-10 hours in.

The core of the issue, I think, is pacing.  After playing quite a bit of this game, I replayed Chrono Trigger, which does just about everything this game does (with a lighter tone of course) and outperforms it in every way, especially pacing.  You're through Chrono Trigger with a satisfying ending in like 15 hours.  Truthfully, I was done with E33 at about that 15 hour mark, but it promises more and more and I didn't feel like it delivered, personally.  Maybe comparing this game to Chrono Trigger is unfair, but it did have the benefit of coming a long time after, and many people consider E33 a masterpiece.

Speaking of pacing, I'll wrap up this review by saying I think you should get this game on sale and play it until you're satisfied, but not necessarily to its conclusion.  The developer is doing some interesting stuff and I'd be excited to learn about what they're cooking up next.  Just as long as it's a bit shorter than E33.

CO:E33 IMO is one of the games everyone has a positive opinion of, me included, but I just dont buy into calling it one of the best of all time, it was a really solid 8-9 outta 10 game made by very experienced developers. 
I had already wishlisted the game months before release because it looked like a very interesting turn-based game. but once you play it you will realise(given that you have played a lot of turn based strategy games before) it is  always your turn so its not a proper 'turn'-based game. 

Gameplay - The game awards precise timed parries and learning the patterns of enemy attacks to hit massive counterattack damage.  Dodge is also there as an defensive option but it is not good enough since parries give you that sweet counter damage. Here is my issue the weakest parts of the combat are the skills itself, Elements and Weakness dont matter since you can just parry off your mistakes and still deal more damage to the enemy than what you healed them for. Pictos and Luminas are way too OP specially after that massive damage spike you get after Act II. genuinely 5/10 for me definitely my least favorite part.

Exploration: Although The world Itself is very beautiful, it feels very disjointed, looks like they just arranged every thing randomly at random locations, I am not a fan of the miniaturised areas full of loading screens. although the world is beautifull at a glance most of it is not accessible (I guess they did the most they could in a AA budget). However every location during main story is very beautifully designed 

*Spoilers Alert*

Story and Characters: Till the end of Act 2 the story was perfect everything just seemed perfect, After that it felt very rushed (personally), I genuinely cannot express how lackluster it felt to me after having an almost flawless Act 2.  The game takes a very Cinematic Approach and Voice acting are very good in both French and English. All the characters are lovable ( looking at you Sciel) and all of their personalities are very different, like i could tell from the very body language and dialogue style of Verso that he was a liar.

SFX and Music: Music is pretty top notch I'd say the main thing that will capture you. go give " Flying waters- Goblu" a listen, you can feel why the develepers took insipiration from JRPGs, the music is also very comparable to  JRPG music. SFX are just normal nothing special i'd say, the only sounds you should care about is the one where you need to parry.

Difficulty: this game does require a few skills to play which are keen eye and ears which will help you time your parries perfectly, lowering difficulty increases parry window and changes the amount of  damage dealt/received.

So basically if you are into more cinematic experience and narrative this is the game for you, or you like parry based games you will not be dissappointed. But those who enjoy strategic Turn- Based RPGs may not enjoy it as much 

I rate it 8/10
